seed: hand-authored bespoke cross-domain case: Meridian transport OSS vs Cascade IP/VPN controller, adjacent domains overlapping only at the transport-underlay seam
note: Gold for the cross-domain configuration case. Correspondences are the correct cross-model concept pairs at the seam. false_cognates are lexically tempting pairs that must NOT be proposed — here the cross-domain 'grade' trap, where one word denotes unrelated things. residual is the per-side native concepts with no counterpart. verification is by worked provisioning and read-back, since with no standard and two domains nothing looks alike to round-trip.

false_cognates.why: both are labelled 'grade' but denote unrelated things: a Meridian grade is a transport protection/restoration class of a circuit; a Cascade grade is an IP class of service (scheduling and drop priority). They share no reference category and must not be corresponded — the cross-domain false cognate the ad-hoc reference is built to pre-empt.

b_only.closure: IP-native service; the transport side knows only the circuit that underlays it

verification_by_placement.both_cognitive: worked provisioning and read-back: run one order through the exchange, provision it, and read the instance back to confirm every pinned requirement is honoured
verification_by_placement.one_inert: provisioning read-back on the live side; pinned-requirement evidence on the inert side
verification_by_placement.both_inert: external adjudication or a downstream provisioning test
